## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `adopt` branch needs the same equality guard that `replace` has: as written, adopting an unchanged value reports a change and rewrites the configuration file.

## Changes
This pull request adds an `adopt` flag to `merge` in `app/config.py`. With the flag set, every existing key is overwritten with the incoming value and recorded in the change list. The pull request also adds tests for adopting a key and for replacing a key whose value differs.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — Skip adoption when the existing value already matches — Calling `merge(path, {"theme": "dark"}, adopt=True)` on a file that already holds `{"theme":"dark"}` returns `["theme"]` and rewrites the file with `indent=2`, because the `adopt` branch never compares `current[key] != value`. The module docstring promises to preserve "untouched configuration files", and `replace` keeps that promise through its guard at line 19. Because `adopt` is checked before `replace`, a call with both flags set also loses the byte-preservation that `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes` protects. — Adopt runs reformat unchanged config files and report false changes to callers that act on the change list. — Fix: Wrap lines 14–15 in `if current[key] != value:`, as the `replace` branch does, and add an adopt case modeled on `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes`.
